PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Make Agent Merge enablement experiment configurable
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- allow experiments to override the default value of `chat.agentMerge.enabled`
- use automatic experiment updates so the resolved value continues to sync through the existing Agent Host configuration bridge

## Testing

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostStarter.config.contribution.ts`
- `npm run typecheck-client`

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup resolves experimental configuration defaults and initializes the Agent Merge setting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution runs in BlockRestore and awaits treatment resolution before the defaults pass completes. The added setting contributes one treatment lookup, but the assignment service already initializes TAS and other experimental settings already await the same shared initial fetch; Agent Host connection later forwards the existing full root-config patch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared initial fetch per assignment-service setup, independent of the number of experimental settings; the added setting does not add another fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The assignment service and other experimental settings already initialized and awaited the same TAS fetch; this setting itself was not queried.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold getTreatment can await the shared initial fetch during default resolution, but the same defaults pass already resolves many experimental settings and therefore already awaited it before this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward full mirrored root configuration to the Agent Host on connect/reconnect
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root-config action per Agent Host client connection/reconnection, with the Agent Merge key already present before this diff because its agentHost descriptor is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Agent Merge setting was already mirrored in the full root-config patch using its product-quality default or user value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs on Agent Host connection, not per treatment lookup; the diff can alter the value in the existing patch but does not add another action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered experimental settings; this diff adds one setting to that collection. Network cardinality remains one shared TAS initial fetch rather than one fetch per setting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Experimental settings are resolved sequentially through one Throttler task. TAS initialization and its initial fetch are shared/cached across all getTreatment calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold assignment cache, the first treatment lookup may await the already-started initial TAS fetch; subsequent lookups read the initialized client cache. On a warm cache, the added lookup is an in-memory treatment read plus existing telemetry. No new cache or key-retention lifecycle is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed schema adds one getTreatment call to an existing sequential defaults pass, while assignmentService explicitly shares initialization and conditionally awaits only the first network fetch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup timing of the shared TAS initial fetch varies by cache and network, but the diff does not increase fetch cardinality or create a new boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup gains only one cached treatment resolution/telemetry event, with no additional network or Agent Host IPC cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hourly or filter-driven assignment refresh re-resolves the Agent Merge experiment while its value is unchanged
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing TAS poll/filter refresh completes first, then onDidRefetchAssignments queues one coalesced Throttler task over all auto settings. The Agent Merge treatment is read from the initialized TAS client. Equality against the registered experimental default exits before configuration registry mutation, Agent Host IPC, or filesystem persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing TAS refetch per one-hour poll or relevant filter change; adding an auto setting does not change request count or payload fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: TAS already auto-polled and emitted assignment-context updates for the many existing auto experiments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network request precedes the configuration re-resolution and was already present; the added setting is not responsible for initiating an extra request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for an unchanged treatment because no configuration delta event is produced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Agent Host action occurred absent a configuration change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist Agent Host root configuration JSON
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for an unchanged treatment because no RootConfigChanged action is dispatched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No write occurred absent a root-config action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Refresh frequency (normally once per hour plus filter/account/override changes) and number of auto experimental settings; this diff adds one O(1) lookup per refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh processing is serialized/coalesced by the configuration contribution's Throttler. The added treatment lookup is awaited in the existing sequential loop; it does not launch concurrent boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: After TAS initialization, getTreatment reads the in-memory client value. Identical values are explicitly deduplicated by registeredExperimentalDefaults equality before deltaConfiguration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the one-hour interval, Throttler, in-memory treatment read after initialization, and equality suppression are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filter-change events may vary by installation, but unchanged values stay behind the equality guard and the extra work remains one cached lookup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: steady-state refreshes add only a single cached lookup and do not fan out across IPC, filesystem, or sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: An assignment transition changes chat.agentMerge.enabled while VS Code and Agent Host are running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an existing TAS refetch, the defaults contribution applies one changed experimental default. Each connected Agent Host client mirrors one key in one RootConfigChanged action. The host serializes one root-config persistence write, then reconciles loaded sessions; enabling also restores the indexed set of explicitly Agent-Merge-enabled persisted sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: TAS refetch that supplies the changed assignment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing refetch per poll/filter trigger, not one per setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same TAS polling boundary existed, but its result did not control this setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the changed treatment can apply, but was not introduced by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch changed Agent Merge root configuration to each connected Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per connected Agent Host protocol client for an actual setting transition; no per-session IPC is emitted solely by the bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Merge enablement changed through product defaults or explicit user configuration, not automatic assignment updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Applies the new experiment value live; this path is newly reachable from an assignment transition, while it already existed for user/default configuration changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and write the Agent Host root-config values
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized write per received root-config action/host on an actual treatment transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No write was caused by an experiment transition for this setting; the same write path handled user-driven changes and other mirrored settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued after the in-memory root action; it does not block configuration processing, and writes cannot overlap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the Agent Merge enabled-session index, then inspect/restore indexed sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One index query plus bounded per-indexed-session lookups/database opens; only explicitly monitored sessions are included, already-loaded sessions are skipped, and concurrency is capped at four.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bounded restore occurred when enablement was turned on through existing configuration paths, but an experiment could not trigger it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously only when the treatment transitions to enabled so monitoring resumes as required; it is not on general editor input/render/startup paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create background GitHub pull-request subscriptions and perform authoritative refreshes for restored monitored sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one subscription/refresh per restored, explicitly Agent-Merge-enabled session; restoration concurrency is capped at four and non-monitored history is excluded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Occurred when the user/product configuration enabled Agent Merge and restored the same indexed sessions, but not from an experiment transition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background feature work required to resume monitoring after enablement; not on the configuration update's synchronous critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of connected Agent Host clients/windows, loaded session URIs, and persisted sessions explicitly indexed as Agent Merge enabled. The restore does not enumerate the full session registry and limits materialization concurrency to four.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration refetches are Throttler-serialized. Root-config writes are chained serially. Persisted-session restore is serialized through _agentMergeRestore and bounded by Limiter(4). Per-host loaded-session notification/reconciliation loops are synchronous but occur only on an actual treatment transition.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Treatment values come from the refreshed in-memory TAS state. Identical treatments are suppressed; only a changed value reaches the bridge. The persisted enabled-session index narrows restore work, and already-materialized sessions are skipped.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line makes runtime assignment transitions authoritative for this setting, and the traced bridge, persistence, loaded-session loops, indexed restore, limiter, and background GitHub refresh are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of open windows and explicitly monitored sessions varies, and treatment transitions are remotely controlled; exact I/O cost is therefore deployment-dependent. Effective cardinality is nevertheless bounded to connected clients and the indexed monitored-session set.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance bug: boundary work occurs only when the experiment genuinely changes feature enablement, is required to realize that behavior, suppresses unchanged polls, uses a narrow persisted index, serializes writes, and caps restore concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and traced startup resolution, steady-state assignment refresh, changed-treatment propagation, Agent Host IPC/persistence, loaded-session reconciliation, indexed restore, and background GitHub monitoring. The diff adds one cached treatment lookup per refresh and intentionally makes real enablement transitions reach existing bounded/coalesced Agent Merge activation paths; no high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.
